findings.requirement: US-29: «Архив, охватывающий обновление мажорной версии: смена числа колонок в середине архива — известный дефект, существующий и сегодня; в этой фиче не исправляется и не усугубляется»
findings.detail: Decision 5b adds a mixed-width diff guard to internal/stat/postgres.go — the shared diff engine used by top, record and report — for exactly the edge case the user-spec lists under «Граничные случаи» and explicitly excludes from this feature. Its rationale is that the feature creates the reachability ('That was unreachable while every view had one fixed width'), which does not hold on three independent counts. (1) report/report.go:250: `if !prevStat.Valid || prevMeta.version != d.meta.version { ...; continue }` — when the archive's metadata version changes, the previous snapshot is discarded and the view is re-Configured, so a diff pair never spans a version boundary in replay; the major-upgrade archive scenario cannot reach the indexing. (2) internal/query/bgwriter.go:41 SelectStatBgwriterQuery already returns 12/13/14 columns for PG14/17/18, and io.go:87 does the same — version-dependent Ncols has existed since [004]/[006], so mixed-width archives were representable long before this feature; the user-spec is right that the defect exists today. (3) top/top.go:63 is the only non-test Configure() call — neither top nor record reconfigures mid-session, so no live path produces a width change between consecutive snapshots either. What remains is a fix for a pre-existing defect the user explicitly deferred, in a production file the Architecture section does not list, with blast radius across every view rather than the three progress screens. This is also inconsistent with the tech-spec's own Decision 7, which declines to fix a pre-existing coverage hole precisely because it would be scope creep. Secondary defect: Decision 5b's Alternatives cite 'the `Aligned`-flag issue noted in Backward Compatibility', but the Backward Compatibility section contains no such note — a dangling cross-reference. Fix: drop Decision 5b and the guard from Task 6, or take the scope change back to the user for explicit approval with the corrected premise.

findings.requirement: Architecture → «What we're building/modifying» must enumerate the production files the feature touches
findings.detail: Task 6 lists `internal/stat/postgres.go` under Files to modify (the Decision 5b guard), but the Architecture file inventory does not mention it — it stops at query.go, postgres/testing.go, the three progress query files, view/view.go, report/describe.go and the CI/image files. A reader of the Architecture section would conclude the diff engine is untouched. This stands independently of how the Decision 5b question is resolved: if the guard stays, the file belongs in the inventory; if it goes, Task 6's Files to modify must lose it.

summary: 27/28 requirements covered, 1 partial (US-29, addressed contrary to instruction), 0 missing. Round-1 findings are all confirmed closed: probe sequencing (Wave 1 now holds Task 1 alone, Task 2 moved to Wave 2), breakage routing (Risks table carries the user-spec policy verbatim — fix here, except where a later feature of the same release re-enters the area, named in the QA report, returns here if that feature drops out — and Task 10 routes findings through it), the 27-screen walk (Task 10 now names both pg_stat_io sub-screens, all seven pg_stat_statements sub-screens, all six progress screens and the local-connection requirement for per-process, with Verify 'bash + user — full QA per the user-spec Как проверить section', which reaches the «Пользователь проверяет» width check), and the deferred items (new subsection carries delay_time, the beta apt channel removal at GA, the nine-test coverage hole and the [014] `mode` name-collision handoff). Of the two security-audit decisions, 5a (beta apt channel pinning) is NOT scope creep: it directly serves the user-spec requirement to install PG 19 from pgdg-testing without disturbing PG 14–18 and mitigates the user-spec risk 'пересборка образа ломает PG 14–18 по причинам, не связанным с фичей'. 5b (mixed-width diff guard) IS scope creep — critical: the user-spec names this exact edge case as a known pre-existing defect explicitly not fixed here, and the tech-spec's counter-claim that the feature makes it reachable is contradicted by report.go:250 (prev snapshot discarded on version change), by bgwriter.go/io.go already having version-dependent Ncols, and by top/record configuring the view exactly once. Remaining scope discipline is clean (repack/data_checksums screens, WAL/slot/stats_reset columns, standby stand, delay_time and README all correctly excluded; the ubuntu:24.04 migration correctly appears only as a Risks ladder rung, not as a task). Solution and Architecture carry real substance (selector idiom, Configure() seam, the DiffIntvl silent-corruption argument); no overengineering in the task set — tasks are scope descriptions without pseudocode.
